| Tool | Exact version used | Why this version | Install command |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python (backend) | 3.12 in the image (`python:3.12-slim`). The developer machine's venv runs 3.14.3, and `__pycache__` holds cpython-312 and cpython-314 files, so both work. | The production image is the reference. Workflows SDK compatibility was tested on 3.12. | `py -3.12 -m venv .venv` (Windows) or `python3.12 -m venv .venv`, then `pip install -r requirements.txt cryptography` |
| Python (Tool Service) | 3.11 (`python:3.11-slim`) | The image's base. The sandbox runs the same interpreter. | Docker is recommended; locally `python3.11 -m venv .venv && pip install -r requirements.txt -r sandbox_requirements.txt ruff` |
| mistralai SDK | 2.8.0 (`>=2.6.0` backend, `>=2.8.0` Tool Service) | `reasoning_effort` and the Agents, Conversations and Workflows APIs need 2.x. `mistralai-workflows` needs `<3.0.0,>=2.4.2`. | Via requirements |
| mistralai-workflows | 3.4.0 (with temporalio 1.24.0) | Only needed to run published workflows (the worker) | `pip install mistralai-workflows` (the image does this when `WITH_MISTRAL_WORKFLOWS=true`) |
| Node.js | 22 (`node:22-slim`; developer machine v22.17.1) | Vite 8 and TanStack Start need a current LTS | nvm or the installer |
| bun | 1.x (`oven/bun:1` in the Dockerfile) | `frontend-3/bun.lock` is the lock file | `npm i -g bun` or the bun installer. `npm install` also works but ignores `bun.lock`. |
| Docker Engine and Compose v2 | Any current version | Neo4j locally; the whole stack in production | Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or `deploy/azure/vm-setup.sh` on Ubuntu |
| Neo4j | 5 community (`neo4j:5-community`) | Graph RAG; the Cypher used targets 5.x | `docker compose up -d neo4j` at the repo root |
| Caddy | 2 (`caddy:2-alpine`) | Production reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS | Via `deploy/docker-compose.yml` |
| OpenSSH client | Any | `ssh -G` for remote servers (in the backend image) | apt `openssh-client` |
| Brev CLI | Latest (fetched at image build) | Only for NVIDIA Brev remote servers | `WITH_BREV_CLI=true` build argument; on Windows, inside WSL (`BREV_WSL_DISTRO`) |
| Azure CLI | Any | Only for `deploy/azure/create-vm.sh` | `az` installer |
| git | Any | Clone; `.gitattributes` forces LF | n/a |

## Operating system notes
- **Windows (the primary development OS):**
  - the worker supervisor uses `signal.signal` handlers instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, and `terminate()` instead of SIGTERM (`mistral_worker.py`);
  - the Brev CLI must run inside WSL; the backend calls it through `wsl`, unless `BREV_NATIVE` is set;
  - `chmod 600` on generated key files is best effort and does nothing on Windows;
  - PowerShell's default encoding breaks some scripts' Unicode output; set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`.
- **Line endings:** `.gitattributes` forces LF. Shell scripts in `deploy/` fail with CRLF.
- **Paths:** `MISTRAL_WORKFLOWS_DIR=../mistral_workflows` is relative to `backend/`. In the container the same layout is reproduced (`/srv/backend` next to `/srv/mistral_workflows`), so start the backend from `backend/`.
- **Sandbox:** the Tool Service demotes generated code to `sandboxuser` and applies rlimits. That only works on Linux as root, so run the Tool Service in Docker. On Windows or macOS without Docker, the sandbox limits are weaker or unavailable (see `synthesis/sandbox.py`).
- **SQLite file locking:** WAL mode creates `sql_app.db-wal` and `-shm`. Do not put the database on a network share.
- **Case sensitivity:** route and file names are lower-case. TanStack's file routes depend on exact names (`agents.$id.tsx`).

## Hardware and quotas
- **Production VM:** the Azure default is Standard_D4s_v5 (4 vCPU, 16 GiB). `DEPLOYMENT.md` says not to go below 8 GiB of RAM. Neo4j alone takes up to 1.5 GiB (512 MB page cache plus 1 GB heap). `vm-setup.sh` adds 4 GB of swap.
- **Disk:** small. SQLite databases, uploads (20 MB per file maximum), generated tools, Neo4j data and Docker images (several GB).
- **No GPU** is needed; every model runs at Mistral.
- **Mistral quotas:**
  - planning makes many parallel calls (up to `DECISION_CONCURRENCY` 6 per key, and 5 facet layers at once), so the key's rate limit must allow several concurrent requests;
  - 429s are retried with backoff (4 retries);
  - each workspace uses its own key and quota;
  - the account needs access to the models in use: mistral-medium-2604, mistral-large-4, mistral-medium-latest, mistral-large-latest, magistral-medium-latest, mistral-small-latest, mistral-embed, mistral-ocr-latest and voxtral-mini-latest;
  - it also needs access to the Agents, Libraries, Connectors and Workflows (beta) APIs.
